name: Donn Bó

attributes.attribute: slew and decapitated by his killer
head sang a beautiful, piercing melody at the victory banquet

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Donn Bó was an Irish hero. He sang sweetly. He was young. His killer slew him and cut off his head. This decapitation followed custom. The killer took the head to a victory banquet. He set the head on a pillar. The head began to sing. The melody was fair and piercing. Everyone in the hall wept.

okr.objective: Records Donn Bó, a young Irish warrior whose severed head sang a moving melody at a victory banquet.
key_results: Donn Bó was famous for his sweet singing.
His killer slew and decapitated him, according to custom.
The head was displayed on a pillar at the victory banquet.
The head sang a piercingly beautiful melody.
Everyone in the hall was reduced to tears.
